notes.summary: The algebraic kernel passes at the reduced degree-n convention: all power/product laws, primary integral-closure invariance, and monotonicity using simultaneous superficial choices in the SAME quotients. Arbitrary residue fields and embedded/nonpure quotients are retained.
notes.detailedSummary: For excellent reduced local R of dimension n>=1, mixed multiplicities use the degree-n part of primary-product length polynomials. Powers and products follow from labelled-variable substitution, with unused labels justified by a fixed-exponent squeeze. Integral-closure invariance follows from finite graded Rees-module exponent errors and equality of entire leading forms. Monotonicity uses simultaneous superficial elements for both families, identical successive quotients, stabilized colon formulas and one-dimensional Samuel inequalities. The proof does not infer coefficient inequalities merely from polynomial domination.
notes.text:
Let A be excellent local and R=A_red, of dimension n>=1. Fix a proper primary gauge a. Qualified G331 supplies the compact Hausdorff section X_a of ALL centered semivaluations, the geometric classes C and D, primary-function density and the all-support primary integral-dependence criterion. No operator or intersection theorem is imported.

Use the degree-n homogeneous part H of the published polynomial length_R(M/(I_1^s_1...I_r^s_r)M). With n separately labelled ideals, e_R(I_1,...,I_n;M) is the coefficient of s_1...s_n. A coefficient of general type d is divided by d_1!...d_r!. Modules of dimension below n contribute zero. A unit label makes the length function independent of that variable, so any mixed coefficient containing a unit slot is zero. Repeated labels agree with this convention: substituting s_1+...+s_n into e(I)s^n/n! gives coefficient e(I).

Symmetry follows by relabelling. Substitution s↦ls proves e(I^l,K_2,...,K_n)=l e(I,K_2,...,K_n) for every positive integer l. For products, use n+1 labelled ideals I,J,K_2,...,K_n and substitute the same s for the I and J variables. Only exponent types (1,0,1,...,1) and (0,1,1,...,1) contribute to s s_2...s_n. Hence e(IJ,K_2,...,K_n)=e(I,K_2,...,K_n)+e(J,K_2,...,K_n).

Here is the needed unused-label justification. Fix its exponent at a sufficiently large c. If B is that primary ideal, B^c contains a power K^N of a remaining primary ideal. For the remaining product P, P K^N⊂B^c P⊂P. The two outside length polynomials have identical top forms because their exponents differ by a constant shift. Squeezing along every positive rational ray identifies the middle top form with the polynomial having B omitted. Iteration proves all product/power laws, including repeated and unused labels.

Suppose I⊂J and J is integral over I. The graded algebra R[Jt] is finite over R[It]: each generator jt satisfies a homogeneous ideal-integrality equation. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most c. Degree m+c then gives J^(m+c)⊂I^m. Thus for m>c and every remaining primary product P,
I^m P⊂J^m P⊂I^(m-c)P.
The outside length polynomials have the same degree-n form and differ by O(t^(n-1)) along each positive rational ray. The middle form therefore agrees on every such ray, hence identically. All mixed coefficients agree. If I and J have the same integral closure, I+J is integral over each; apply this argument twice. This is equality of leading FORMS, not coefficientwise inference from an inequality.

For monotonicity, take J⊂I primary and fix K_2,...,K_n. If the residue field is finite, pass to T=R[z]_(mR[z]). This faithfully flat local extension has residue field k(z). Tensoring a finite composition series preserves its length: every residue factor becomes k(z). Dimension is preserved as well. A parameter ideal with n generators remains mT-primary and gives dim T≤n by the height theorem; flat going-down lifts a length-n chain ending at m to one ending at mT and gives dim T≥n. Consequently the primary-product polynomials and their mixed coefficients are unchanged. No valuation-space base-change claim is used.

Over the infinite residue field, Proposition 17.2.2 supplies simultaneous nonempty open choices in K_n/mK_n for the two families (K_n,J,K_2,...,K_(n-1)) and (K_n,I,K_2,...,K_(n-1)). Exclude all minimal primes of the SAME current ring. Primaryness ensures K_n lies in none of them. Their excluded images are proper linear subspaces by Nakayama. A finite intersection of these opens has a point over the infinite field. Choose ONE lift x and use ONE quotient R/(x) for both families. Its dimension is exactly one less because x avoids all minimal primes.

The full superficial colon statement and multi-ideal Artin–Rees give, for large exponents, (P_s:x)=(0:x)+the product with one K_n exponent removed, and (0:x)∩P_s=0. Thus (0:x) injects into a finite primary quotient and has finite length. The multiplication-by-x exact sequence identifies the discrete first difference of the length polynomial with the quotient length polynomial minus length(0:x). In dimension d>1 that constant does not affect the degree d-1 part. Comparing coefficients proves the reduction formula for BOTH families in the SAME quotient. Embedded primes require no assumed regular sequence: the actual stabilized colon formula controls them.

Repeat with K_(n-1),...,K_2 in the common successive quotients. These quotients may be nonreduced or embedded, but the source applies to arbitrary Noetherian local rings. The final common quotient R' has dimension one, and the compared numbers become e_R'(JR') and e_R'(IR'). The one-variable inequalities length(R'/(JR')^s)≥length(R'/(IR')^s) prove e_R'(JR')≥e_R'(IR'). Ordinary one-dimensional multiplicity also gives positive integer mixed multiplicities for proper entries. For n=1 this argument is direct. Symmetry gives every slot, and integral-closure invariance gives closure monotonicity.

A positive-dimensional LOCAL ring has no zero-dimensional minimal component: such a prime would be m, contradicted by any prime strictly below m. Thus G331's zero-component exception is vacuous for our reduced local R. Lower-dimensional components still have zero degree-n contribution. Nilpotent intersection lengths are not substituted for this reduction convention.

Fresh source reading covered complete current July2024 Swanson–Huneke 8.4.2, 17.1.6, 17.2.1–4, 17.4.1–9 and 17.5.1–5 immediate units. The relevant polynomial, superficial and reduction units are applied at their actual hypotheses. Historical Hilbert–Samuel, Artin–Rees, Nakayama and dimension foundations are ordinary published background. Essential formulas were inspected on exact PDF printed pages 140,355,359,360. The proof does not use the terse coefficient-domination argument in 17.5.3 or the displayed intermediate power formula. Indeed (s-t)^2 is nonnegative with a negative st coefficient. No claim of printed error is made merely from extraction.

notes.summary: All-support FUNCTION-dependent rational moments are well-defined and positive. Real extension and compact-Hausdorff Riesz give a unique positive Radon measure with exact n-1 potential arity and reference mass.
notes.detailedSummary: Equality of scaled ideal profiles on the whole boundary implies equality of integral closures and therefore equal mixed moments. Cross-product relations prove rational test representation independence. Closure monotonicity proves positivity; constants bound the functional in the supremum norm. Density, a proved positive real extension, and Riesz yield the measure. This establishes function independence, not the unresolved geometric Cartier intersection comparison.
notes.text:
Put p=n-1. For rational profiles u_i=-v(I_i)/k_i define B_u(v(J))=e_R(I_1,...,I_p,J)/(k_1...k_p). For p=0 this is e_R(J), with empty denominator 1. Units represent zero; for p>=1 a unit in any potential slot annihilates the moment. N1 proves rational positive homogeneity and addition in each nonpositive input slot.

If -v(I)/k=-v(I')/k' on ALL X_a, then I^k' and (I')^k have equal values there. G331's exact criterion gives equal integral closures; n1's invariance and power law give equal moments. Similarly u≤u' gives I^k'⊂overline((I')^k), hence B_u(v(J))≥B_u'(v(J)). These statements depend on FUNCTIONS on the whole boundary, including nonminimal supports.

Every rational test combination is (v(J)-v(K))/d, with J,K unit-or-primary. If this equals (v(J')-v(K'))/d', then the products J^d'(K')^d and K^d'(J')^d have equal values. If proper, their integral closures agree. If one is a unit, equality forces both to be units because primary values are strictly positive on nonempty X_a. Product/power additivity therefore makes the proposed test value independent of both representations and proves rational linearity.

If f=(v(J)-v(K))/d≥0, then J⊂overline K when K is proper. N1 gives B(v(J))≥B(v(K)). When K is a unit, nonnegativity gives the same conclusion; J unit and K proper cannot satisfy the hypothesis. Thus the functional is positive on the entire rational test lattice.

The constant 1 is v(a). For rational q>||f||, positivity on q1±f gives |B(f)|≤qB(1). Taking q down to ||f|| gives the norm bound. G331 supplies uniform density in the REAL space C(X_a). Extend by uniform limits; continuity extends rational scaling to real scaling. Positivity also extends: for h≥0 choose lattice f_j within epsilon_j of h and rational r_j>epsilon_j tending to zero. Then f_j+r_j≥0, so B(f_j)≥-r_j B(1); the limit is nonnegative.

Compact-Hausdorff Riesz–Markov now gives a unique finite positive Radon measure. No metrizability assumption is needed. Its exact mass is e_R(I_1,...,I_p,a)/(k_1...k_p). The test supplies the nth multiplicity entry, so the potential arity is exactly n-1. Function independence covers different G331 geometric presentations with the same evaluation, but does not prove equality with a separately defined geometric intersection.

notes.summary: The measures extend uniquely to C by uniform approximation, with a negative-constant shift estimate, bounded masses and weak uniform-input continuity. No general singular multiplier theorem is used.
notes.detailedSummary: For inputs in [-M,0], ideal-test moments are bounded by M^p e(a,...,a,J), and uniform perturbations epsilon have error at most ((M+epsilon)^p-M^p) times that reference multiplicity. The estimate makes every rational approximation independent and gives positive functional limits. Dense tests and uniformly bounded masses prove weak convergence for arbitrary uniform input nets. Total-variation continuity is not claimed.
notes.text:
Write E_J=e_R(a,...,a,J), with p copies of a, and E_a=e_R(a). Comparing rational inputs in [-M,0] with -M v(a) gives 0≤B_u(v(J))≤M^p E_J and mass≤M^p E_a. For real M use rational upper bounds decreasing to M. For p=0 the factor is 1, even at M=0; for p>=1 and M=0 all inputs and the measure are zero.

If two rational tuples u,w lie in [-M,0] and their coordinatewise uniform distances are at most epsilon, then u-epsilon≤w and w-epsilon≤u. The negative-constant shift expansion is
B_(u-epsilon)(v(J))-B_u(v(J))
=Σ_(nonempty S) epsilon^|S| B_(inputs -v(a) in S, u elsewhere)(v(J)).
Every term is nonnegative and at most epsilon^|S| M^(p-|S|)E_J. Thus, using rational epsilon slightly above the norm difference when necessary,
|B_u(v(J))-B_w(v(J))|≤Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J,
where Delta_p(M,epsilon)=(M+epsilon)^p-M^p and Delta_0=0.

Choose rational primary-profile approximations to any tuple in C using G331's exact uniform density. They lie in a common bounded interval. The estimate makes every ideal-test moment Cauchy; comparing two approximation choices crosswise proves the same limit. Rational-difference test limits are linear, positive and mass bounded. N2's real extension and Riesz argument yields the unique measure on C.

Symmetry, addition and nonnegative REAL scaling pass through approximations. Order passes by comparing approximants after a 2eta negative shift and letting eta tend to zero. The same bound and perturbation estimate hold on C. No envelope or multiplier approximation is needed here.

Under any uniform input net, ideal-test moments and masses converge. For an arbitrary continuous test f, choose a rational-difference test h within eta. Each integral error is bounded by eta times the corresponding mass. The common mass bound and convergence on h prove convergence on f. This is weak continuity, not total-variation continuity.

notes.summary: Every bounded actual decreasing C representation gives the same measure. Actual bounded decreasing D-net weak continuity is proved when its specified limit belongs to D, without nested-net flattening or increasing D closure.
notes.detailedSummary: Scalar ideal moments increase along finite products of actual C representations and remain bounded. Compact directed strict open covers compare any two representations up to negative shifts, proving independence and the C-majorant supremum formula. D addition, order and shift laws are established before the decreasing-D-net step. Upper-semicontinuous open covers then give exact moment convergence and weak convergence. Limit membership in D remains a hypothesis.
notes.text:
Let bounded u_i∈D satisfy -M≤u_i≤0. Choose ACTUAL decreasing C-nets g_(i,alpha) with infimum u_i. Every term already lies in [-M,0]. Their finite product index set is directed. For every primary J the scalar moments B_g(v(J)) INCREASE and are bounded by M^p E_J. Their finite supremum defines the ideal-test limit. Differences, linearity, positivity and the mass bound pass through these scalar limits; Riesz gives a positive Radon measure. Dense tests and bounded masses also give weak convergence of the representing measures.

For full representation independence, take another actual representation f_(i,beta). Fix beta and epsilon>0. For each coordinate the continuous open sets {g_(i,alpha)<f_(i,beta)+epsilon} increase and cover compact X_a because inf_alpha g_(i,alpha)=u_i≤f_(i,beta). A finite subcover and an upper bound of its indices give one alpha working everywhere. Finite product indices handle all coordinates simultaneously. Hence g_alpha-epsilon≤f_beta and
B_fbeta(v(J))≤B_(galpha-epsilon)(v(J))
≤B_galpha(v(J))+Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J
≤sup_alpha B_galpha(v(J))+Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J.
Let epsilon decrease to zero, then take sup_beta. Interchanging the representations gives equality. Density gives equality of the measures. This works for arbitrary directed sets and nonmetrizable compact boundaries.

The same cover argument works with any fixed C-majorant tuple h_i≥u_i. Such h_i also lie in [-M,0]. It gives B_h(v(J))≤B_u(v(J)). Conversely representing tuples are C-majorants. Therefore
B_u(v(J))=sup{B_h(v(J)):h_i∈C, h_i≥u_i}.
If u≤w, the majorants of w are a subset of those of u, so B_u(v(J))≥B_w(v(J)). This is ideal-test moment order; it does not assert order of the resulting measures on every positive continuous test.

Addition in a slot is justified with the finite product of actual C representations of the summands. Their sums form an actual decreasing C representation of the sum; C additivity and scalar limits give D additivity. Scaling and symmetry follow identically. Consequently the real negative-shift expansion holds on D, and 0≤B_(u-epsilon)(v(J))-B_u(v(J))≤Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J.

Now let u_(i,lambda) be an actual coordinatewise decreasing D-net, commonly bounded in [-M,0], with pointwise limit u_i ASSUMED to belong to D. Its moments increase and are at most B_u(v(J)). Fix a C-majorant tuple h of u and epsilon>0. Since u_i,lambda is upper semicontinuous, {u_i,lambda<h_i+epsilon} is OPEN. These sets increase and cover X_a. Compactness and directedness give one common lambda, so u_lambda-epsilon≤h. The already proved D order and shift laws yield
B_h(v(J))≤B_(ulambda-epsilon)(v(J))≤B_ulambda(v(J))+Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J.
Take sup_lambda, then epsilon down to zero, then the supremum over C-majorants h. The majorant formula proves that the increasing scalar limit is exactly B_u(v(J)). Rational difference density and bounded masses give weak convergence on every continuous test.

Only bounded scalar moments take increasing limits. There is no increasing function-class closure, arbitrary infimum closure, nested D-net flattening, unbounded-energy limit, or continuity assertion when the specified limit is not known to lie in D.

notes.summary: One-factor gauge covariance and finite-normalization top-dimensional residue-degree weights pass. Full conductor fibres and explicit d0/d1/unit/zero, reference-mass and reduction conventions are retained.
notes.detailedSummary: Homogeneous inputs divide by d=v_a(b), whereas the measure transforms as T_*(d mu_a), with one factor. Artin–Rees shows normalization preserves degree-n forms, and Artinian composition factors give closed residue-field weights for dimension-n centers only. Curve products have zero potential arity and a fixed weighted branch measure. Empty dimension zero has no multiplicity moment law. Nilpotent lengths and arbitrary finite-map operator calculus are not claimed.
notes.text:
For another primary gauge b, let d(v)=v_a(b) and T(v)=v/d(v). G331 makes d positive continuous, finite and bounded with bounded inverse, and gives u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). Rational ideal profiles have the SAME ideals and denominators in either gauge, and v_b(J)(Tv)=v_a(J)/d. Therefore mu_b and T_*(d mu_a) have identical ideal-test moments: integrating v_b(J) against the latter cancels the single d and gives the same mixed multiplicity quotient. Density and uniqueness prove mu_b=T_*(d mu_a). The factor is ONE, independent of n. Its new mass is the old moment against b. Uniform transport and weighted compact pushforward preserve weak convergence; transported bounded actual representations remain bounded and decreasing. N3 and n4 extend the identity to C and bounded D. Successive gauge weights multiply according to the granted homogeneous cocycle.

Let S be the finite normalization and q its local centers above m. A regular conductor element kills S/R and is nonzero on every minimal component. Every prime in its support admits a strictly smaller minimal prime not containing that element, so its prime chains have dimension at most n-1. Hence dim_R(S/R)<n.

Multi-ideal Artin–Rees on 0→R→S→S/R→0 shows that R∩P_s S is sandwiched between P_s R and P_(s-cvec)R for a fixed exponent vector. The two outside length polynomials have identical top forms. The quotient length exact sequence and the lower dimension of S/R therefore show e_R(I_1,...,I_n;S)=e_R(I_1,...,I_n;R). This does not assume R/P_s injects into S/P_s S.

For every primary product P, the Artinian S-module S/PS decomposes into local-center pieces. An S_q composition factor k(q) has R-length f_q=[k(q):k(m)], a finite positive integer. Thus length_R(S/PS)=Σ_q f_q length_Sq(S_q/PS_q). Comparing degree-n forms gives
e_R(I_1,...,I_n)=Σ_(dim S_q=n) f_q e_Sq(I_1 S_q,...,I_n S_q).
Testing the proposed pushforward against every ideal gauge and using density proves
mu_(R,a)(u)=Σ_(dim S_q=n) f_q rho_(q,*)mu_(S_q,aS_q)(rho_q^*u).
Finite sums and compact pushforward, together with n3 and n4, extend it to all bounded tuples.

Every G331 support and conductor fibre remains in the spaces. Finite conductor value has the granted singleton fibre; infinite conductor value has exactly the granted conductor-quotient identification. Lower-dimensional centers contribute zero TOP-degree multiplicity. No generic degree is invented on vertical components. This normalization identity is not arbitrary finite-map operator functoriality.

For n=1, p=0. Each normal local center is a DVR. Put b_q=ord_q(a)>0. Its normalized point is ord_q/b_q, and its reference mass must be b_q because e_Sq(J)=ord_q(J). Hence mu_(R,a)=Σ_q f_q b_q delta_(ord_q/b_q), with mass e_R(a). Branches are local normal centers, not merely minimal components. Zero-arity locality is tautological, but no general curve Cartier comparison is inferred.

For n=0, the local reduction is a field, the boundary is empty, and its only measure is zero. There is no p=-1 operator or degree-zero multiplicity moment law on that boundary. For p>=1 a zero potential/unit input annihilates the measure; a unit test has zero moment. For p=0 no potential slot exists to annihilate the reference measure. For inputs -t_i v(a), mass is (product_i t_i)e_R(a), with empty product 1.

The theory uses A_red. For A=k[[t]][epsilon]/(epsilon^2), its boundary equals that of k[[t]], but length_A(A/(t^s))=2s rather than s. Reduced boundary data cannot determine this nilpotent multiplicity without extra reference data. Such lengths, unbounded energy and the full P12.6 calculus are unclaimed.

notes.text:
Apply BFJ2008 only at a smooth CLOSED point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, n>=2. G331 identifies our C and D on ALL semivaluations with the appropriate BFJ cone and canonical all-retraction extension. Bottom is separately adjoined and is not bounded. This cone grant supplies no operator theorem.

Freshly read complete BFJ Setting and Section4 immediate units, including 4.1–4.9 and the entire proof of 4.4 with Remark 4.5. Equation (4.3), Proposition 4.6 and Proposition 4.7 give our ideal-test law on the m-section. BFJ defines mixed multiplicity by generic parameter colength. It agrees with our polynomial coefficient: simultaneous general superficial choices form a system of parameters; the regular local ring is Cohen–Macaulay, so it is a regular sequence and Samuel parameter multiplicity equals quotient length. The superficial reduction identifies this with the mixed coefficient. Thus rational profile measures agree, including scaling and zero/unit cases, by dense-test uniqueness.

For a C tuple, rational uniform approximants have the same moments. BFJ4.4 supplies pairing symmetry, addition and order at these smooth hypotheses. Negative-constant shifts therefore give exactly n3's Delta_p(M,epsilon) estimate and mass bound. BFJ moments of the C tuple equal the rational limits defining ours.

For bounded D, take the actual decreasing C representations. Their divisorial coefficients decrease to those of the identified BFJ formal psh functions. BFJ4.4's continuity along decreasing families applies to nets: its proof gives upper semicontinuity in the coefficient topology; order bounds intersection values below by the limit value, and upper semicontinuity forces their infimum to equal it. No sequence cofinal in an arbitrary directed set is assumed. Apply this with fixed test Z(J), reverse sign for the positive ideal gauge, and obtain exactly n4's scalar limits. Dense tests and bounded masses give equality of the whole Radon measures on ALL semivaluations.

General primary gauges follow n5. Smooth DVR and empty dimension-zero cases are direct. The essential multiplier approximation in BFJ4.4 remains explicitly restricted to the published smooth algebraically closed characteristic-zero range. Its historical resolution, multiplier, Ramanujam/Rees and intersection foundations are disclosed ordinary published background, not recursively freshly proved. BFJ4.8 alone is a sequence statement; the actual 4.4 topology argument supplies the net application. BFJ4.9's smooth atomic interpretation is not transferred to singular primary models. Literal classical/CLD radial extension comparisons remain distinct.

notes.text:
The algebraic bounded moment theorem passes this independent reconstruction at its exact hypotheses. Actual general singular/nonnormal Cartier INTERSECTION comparison is UNRESOLVED. G331's independent Cartier positivity and FUNCTION-cone comparison do not supply a degree-n intersection theorem. The fixed PRIMARY section correction gives uniform function approximation, but one still needs a proved comparison between primary leading lengths and actual exceptional Cartier Euler-characteristic intersections, including nonpure and non-Cohen–Macaulay behavior, real coefficients and common-refinement projection. The normalization identity in n5 is an algebraic leading-form identity, not that theorem. A nonprimary conductor value divided by k is not a uniform error.

LOCALITY on open agreement regions in dimension>=2 is separately UNRESOLVED. For bounded geometric tuples u,w equal coordinatewise on an open U⊂X_a, the required conclusion is mu_u|U=mu_w|U. Positive global moment functionals, unique Riesz measures and weak continuity do not prove this. No singular-boundary localized cutoff identity or max-locality argument is supplied. This review provides neither a proof nor a counterexample. Zero-arity curve locality and exact smooth specialization do not remove the general obligation.

Therefore the original P12.4 remains incomplete. Function-presentation independence is proved; full geometric model independence through the correct intersection comparison is not. The supporting measures are not relabelled a solved geometric Monge–Ampère theory. P12.3 envelopes, P12.5 reference/energy/finite-energy limits and P12.6 general geometric finite-map operators remain separate. No arbitrary-model cofinality, nilpotent intersection theory or singular characteristic-zero source transfer is silently introduced. Candidate=false.
